answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on scarce, verifiable work: require each agent to lock a small refundable deposit tied to a unique hardware attestation before it can earn, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Think of it like a ferrous anchor on a shale island — the deposit is heavy to move and easy to verify, and a sybil swarm splitting itself across many shells still has to pay the same anchor cost per identity, which caps how many clones an attacker can profitably field.
